newsitem.title: CHINA: China claims victory in row over human rights.
newsitem.headline: China claims victory in row over human rights.

text.p: Beijing on Thursday hailed as a victory for both China and the Third World the sinking of a resolution in the United Nations to censure its human rights record.
"This is a victory not only for China ... but also a victory for developing countries," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.

China rallied strong support from Third World countries at the United Nations Human Rights Commission in Geneva on Tuesday and defeated a proposed resolution criticising its human rights record and treatment of Tibet.
A total of 27 countries supported China in opposing the motion which had been proposed by Denmark and backed by the United States. Nine countries abstained.
It was the seventh year since 1990 that Western countries failed to achieve even a vote on the issue in the 53-member body despite heavy lobbying.
Shen rebuked Denmark and the United States, saying no country's human rights record was perfect.
"Every country's human rights (record) is not perfect. There exist human rights problems of different degrees even in Denmark and the United States," Shen said.
He urged Denmark to "rectify its mistakes" in future and to opt for "constructive dialogue" rather than confrontation.
China has given Denmark and the Netherlands a diplomatic slap on the wrist by postponing official visits. The Netherlands co-sponsored the resolution.
In Washington, the United States on Wednesday accused the commission of failing the people of China by not voting on the resolution.

The U.S. State Department criticised European and other countries that refused to support the resolution and said China had scored only a "Pyrrhic victory" by getting the commission to adopt a no-action motion on the resolution.
Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Japan and Spain all refrained from from officially co-sponsoring the resolution.
